name: Ascension Day
description: Jesus ascends to heaven and gives the Great Commission.
biblicalBasis: Forty days after the resurrection, Jesus ascends to heaven from the Mount of Olives (Acts 1:6-11). He gives the disciples the promise: "You will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you, and you will be my witnesses to the ends of the earth." Two men in white robes say: "This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come back in the same way." The Great Commission: "All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. Go therefore and make disciples of all nations" (Matt 28:18-20). Luke 24:50-53: Jesus blesses them and ascends.
significance: The Ascension does not mean that Jesus leaves the world, but that he reigns from God's right hand with all authority. Christ is not gone — he is present everywhere through the Spirit. The Great Commission is the consequence: because all authority has been given to him, the gospel must reach all people. The promise of the Spirit fills the waiting period with expectation, not emptiness.
liturgicalContext: White color. Celebrated on Thursday (40 days after Easter). Public holiday in many countries. In some traditions, the Paschal candle is extinguished this day as a symbol of Jesus' visible absence. The ten days between Ascension and Pentecost are a time of prayer.
history: Ascension Day has been known as a separate celebration since the 4th century (earlier celebrated together with Pentecost). Augustine calls it one of the oldest Christian festivals. In the Middle Ages, dramatic presentations became common in which a figure of Christ was raised through a hole in the church ceiling.
otConnections: Elijah's ascension in a chariot of fire — Elisha takes up Elijah's cloak and receives a double portion of his spirit (2 Kings 2:1-15). A direct parallel: as Elijah ascends and Elisha receives the spirit, Jesus ascends and the disciples receive the Spirit. Psalm 47: "God has gone up with a shout." Psalm 110:1: "Sit at my right hand." Daniel 7:13-14 about the Son of Man who is brought before God and given eternal dominion.

references.reason: The chapter begins with the sending of the disciples with authority and a mission. This is a precursor to the Great Commission that Jesus gives at the Ascension. The theme of being sent out to the nations (verse 18) is central to the liturgy of Ascension Day.
